translationRepairs: When the Yellow River burst at Maying Dam, he joined Minister Wu Jin in supervising repairs. The breach had scarcely been closed when the south bank at Yifeng gave way again. He was dismissed from office but kept on the works with the nominal rank of department director.

When the Yellow River burst at Maying Dam, he joined Minister Wu Jing in supervising repairs. The breach had scarcely been closed when the south bank at Yifeng gave way again. He was dismissed from office but kept on the works with the nominal rank of department director.
s0006 has 尚書吳璥; 璥 is jing, so Wu Jing is required and Wu Jin is a mistransliteration.

When the Yellow River broke through at Maying Dam, together with Minister Wu Jin he supervised the works; they had just closed the breach when the south bank at Yifeng broke again. He was stripped of office and given the nominal rank of department director while retained on the project.

When the Yellow River broke through at Maying Dam, together with Minister Wu Jing he supervised the works; they had just closed the breach when the south bank at Yifeng broke again. He was stripped of office and given the nominal rank of department director while retained on the project.
The literal likewise misreads 吳璥 as Wu Jin; Wu Jing matches the personal name in the Chinese.

In the seventh year (1827), he proposed reopening the old relief sluice at Wangjiaying and dredging the main channel. When the sluice was closed again, Yellow River water backed up, the control dam had to be shut, and tribute barges had to be worked through the lock in reverse. The court rebuked him for missing his chance; though dismissal was proposed, he was spared and demoted to grand secretary of the Inner Court.

In the seventh year (1827), he proposed reopening the old relief sluice at Wangjiaying and dredging the main channel. When the sluice was closed again, Yellow River water backed up, the control dam had to be shut, and tribute barges had to be worked through the lock in reverse. The court rebuked him for missing his chance; though dismissal was proposed, he was spared and demoted to a bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
降授內閣學士 is demotion to a Grand Secretariat bachelor/academician, not 大學士 grand secretary.

In the seventh year, it was proposed to reopen the old relief sluice at Wangjiaying and dredge the main channel on a large scale; soon afterward, when the relief sluice was sealed again, Yellow River water backed up, the Yellow River control dam was closed once more, and tribute barges had to be emptied and filled in reverse in the lock. An edict rebuked him for missing the moment; dismissal was proposed, but he was spared and demoted to a grand secretary of the Inner Court.

In the seventh year, it was proposed to reopen the old relief sluice at Wangjiaying and dredge the main channel on a large scale; soon afterward, when the relief sluice was sealed again, Yellow River water backed up, the Yellow River control dam was closed once more, and tribute barges had to be emptied and filled in reverse in the lock. An edict rebuked him for missing the moment; dismissal was proposed, but he was spared and demoted to a bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.
Literal also equates 內閣學士 with grand secretary; bachelor of the Grand Secretariat is the correct office.

When news reached the court in the first month of 1841, the emperor was furious. Qi Shan was placed under severe investigation. Prince Yishan was named pacification commissioner, with Minister Long Wen and Hunan commander Yang Fang as deputies, to lead troops to Guangdong.

When news reached the court in the first month of 1841, the emperor was furious. Qi Shan was placed under severe investigation. Beizi Yishan, a grand minister in attendance, was named General for the Pacification of Rebels, with Minister of Revenue Long Wen and Hunan Provincial Military Commander Yang Fang as deputies, to lead troops to Guangdong for joint suppression.
Proposal rightly restores 御前大臣, 貝子, 靖逆將軍, and 戶部尚書, but Beile is 貝勒 not 貝子 (Beizi), 提督 is provincial military commander not regional commander, and 協剿 is omitted.

Censor Chen Qingyong memorialized on the crimes of the officials involved in the affair; the emperor, giving weight to pure opinion, again stripped Qi Shan of office, though he still intended to employ him locally; before long he was given the rank of third-class bodyguard and appointed resident commissioner in Tibet.

Censor Chen Qingyong memorialized on the crimes of the officials involved in the affair; the emperor, giving weight to pure opinion, again stripped Qi Shan of office, though he still intended to employ him; before long he was given the rank of third-class bodyguard and appointed resident commissioner in Tibet.
意仍鄉用/嚮用 means the emperor still meant to employ him; 'locally' invents a place sense absent from the phrase.
Qi Shan was recalled to act as governor of Henan and posted on the Hunan-Henan frontier.
Qi Shan was recalled to act as governor of Henan and posted on the Huguang-Henan frontier.
駐防楚、豫界上 is the Huguang–Henan frontier; narrowing 楚 to Hunan alone is unsupported.
In the third month he beat the rebels repeatedly at Pukou and Leitang, advanced on Yangzhou, and encamped at Baota Hill and Situgong; he won five engagements in a row.
In the third month he beat the rebels repeatedly at Pukou and Leitang, advanced on Yangzhou, and encamped at Baota Hill and Situ Temple; he won five engagements in a row.
司徒廟 is Situ Temple; Situgong misreads 廟 as if it were 宮.
In the third month he repeatedly defeated the rebels at Pukou and Leitang, advanced to suppress Yangzhou, and encamped separately at Baota Hill and Situgong; five battles were all victorious.
In the third month he repeatedly defeated the rebels at Pukou and Leitang, advanced to suppress Yangzhou, and encamped separately at Baota Hill and Situ Temple; five battles were all victorious.
Literal likewise needs Situ Temple for 司徒廟 rather than Situgong.
He rose to grand secretary of the Inner Court and concurrently served as vice commander and commandant of the guards.
He rose to academician of the Grand Secretariat and concurrently served as vice commander and commandant of the guards.
累擢內閣學士 is academician of the Grand Secretariat, distinct from 大學士 grand secretary.
He was promoted in succession to grand secretary of the Inner Court and concurrently served as vice commander and commandant of the guards.
He was promoted in succession to academician of the Grand Secretariat and concurrently served as vice commander and commandant of the guards.
Literal makes the same 內閣學士/大學士 conflation; academician of the Grand Secretariat is correct.

At Qijiang in Sichuan the outlaw Mu Jixian murdered Zhao Yingcai, a military licentiate of Renhuai in Guizhou, then raised a gang and seized Fangjiagou. Yi Libu led Regional Commander Yu Buyun and Provincial Treasurer Qinglu against their stronghold, killing or capturing more than a thousand men and executing the leaders Mu Jixian and Xie Fazhen. The rest were pacified, and he received the double-eyed peacock feather.

At Qijiang in Sichuan the outlaw Mu Jixian murdered Zhao Yingcai, a military licentiate of Renhuai in Guizhou, then raised a gang and seized Fangjiagou. Yi Libu led Provincial Military Commander Yu Buyun and Provincial Administration Commissioner Qinglu against their stronghold, killing or capturing more than a thousand men and executing the leaders Mu Jixian and Xie Fazhen. The rest were pacified, and he received the double-eyed peacock feather.
提督余步雲 is provincial military commander, not regional commander; 布政使慶祿 is provincial administration commissioner.
In the spring of 1842 Expeditionary General Yijing came to relieve Zhejiang and was beaten again.
In the spring of 1842 the General Who Displays Might (Yangwei), Yijing, came to relieve Zhejiang and was beaten again.
揚威將軍 is the campaign title Yangwei / General Who Displays Might, not a generic 'Expeditionary General'.

Qiying and his party met the British commanders Henry Pottinger and Robert Morrison at Jinghai Temple outside Yifeng Gate, signed the treaty, paid six million taels at once with the rest over three years, and peace was concluded.

Qiying and his party met the British commanders Henry Pottinger and Morrison at Jinghai Temple outside Yifeng Gate, signed the treaty, paid six million taels at once with the rest over three years, and peace was concluded.
Chinese only names 馬利遜; inserting the given name Robert invents identity not supported by the text.

Qiying and the others met in alliance with the British generals Henry Pottinger and Robert Morrison at Jinghai Temple outside Yifeng Gate, jointly signed the treaty, paid six million first with the remainder over three years, and peace was concluded.

Qiying and the others met in alliance with the British generals Henry Pottinger and Morrison at Jinghai Temple outside Yifeng Gate, jointly signed the treaty, paid six million first with the remainder over three years, and peace was concluded.
Literal likewise invents Robert for 馬利遜; surname Morrison alone matches the Chinese.

Since the Jiangning peace treaty provided for warehouses in the provincial capital and consuls entering the city, the people of Guangdong still held to the old practice, appealed to the high officials without being understood, then raised militia; public opinion was turbulent and would not submit to official control.

Since the Jiangning peace treaty provided for warehouses in the provincial capital and consuls entering the city, the people of Guangdong still held to the old practice, appealed to the high officials who paid no heed, then raised militia; public opinion was turbulent and would not submit to official control.
愬於大吏，不省 means the high officials paid no heed, not that the appeal was misunderstood.
In 1847 British ships suddenly entered the provincial river with firmer demands. Qiying vaguely promised fulfillment in two years, and they withdrew only after he asked to be punished.
In 1847 British ships suddenly entered the provincial river with firmer demands. Qiying vaguely promised fulfillment in two years; they then withdrew, and he asked to be punished.
謾許…始退，自請議處 sequences withdrawal then self-request for punishment; 'only after he asked to be punished' reverses the causation.

In 1853, as the Taiping rebels advanced north, Qiying's son Qingxi, brigadier at Malan Town, asked that father, sons, and brothers serve at the front together. Qiying was ordered to serve with the patrolling defense commissioners and received the fourth-rank cap button for contributing funds.

In 1853, as the Guangdong rebels advanced north, Qiying's son Qingxi, brigadier at Malan Town, asked that father, sons, and brothers serve at the front together. Qiying was ordered to serve with the patrolling defense commissioners and received the fourth-rank cap button for contributing funds.
粵匪 is Guangdong rebels/bandits; Taiping is an invented proper name absent from the Chinese.
